item.content:encoded:
This seems to be the only SCP by Shaggy with an extant Site-5.

It wasn't there originally. I only added it after putting some thought in to how I plan on developing this SCP throughout the (to be written/released) supplements. I won't say much beside the fact that the next chapter is going to strongly tie this into another one of my SCPs, and hell, maybe by the time all's said and done, maybe we'll learn a thing or two about my version of Site-5.

Should take this time to mention that Site-5 doesn't originate with me, but rather The Great Hippo. For an alternate canonical look at what's going on with the infamous site, I'd check in and see what its progenitor does with it in their 001 Proposal.

item.content:encoded:
The 3540 Incident (forgot to switch the number there to 783) and everything after is a bit of foreshadowing of things still to come.

From the Incident, it's clear that 783 does something to the D-Class that affects not only the still-living victims, but also the deceased (the mass grave being uncovered due to the corpses seizing and moving about). How it all threads together is to be revealed - further investigation will take place in supplementary pieces.

As for the your second point, there is a lot more to the stylistic flair than just the names being messed up if one looks closely. Its subtle, but making it more crazy didn't go over too well with test audiences.

I like it, but I'm confused as to why "Incident 3540.1" and everything after exists. I guess the space shenanigans could be a reference to "—And He Built a Crooked House—" by Robert A. Heinlein, but it comes across to me as the bad kind of vague. The questions that are raised there don't appear to fit in with the rest of the story.

It would make particular sense for this article, since the Foundation has such long stretches where direct research is impossible, and they know next to nothing about the crooked man, so you'd think they would see the benefit of trying to find out what the locals know (or think they know) about the anomaly.

Yea, that makes sense - problem was that while drafting I had a very clear-cut idea of how I wanted it to pace, and I didn't find a good place to stick it in (not to mention, dialogue isn't my strongsuit).

I do beleive I will be adding another supplement to cover this. There's a lot going down that is admittedly glossed over or left to be inferred regarding the role of the townsfolk in the whole scheme of things. I have a couple ideas in mind to develop that.

item.content:encoded: My biggest problem with the piece right now is that it feels unfinished. A monster preying on a small town for years provides opportunities for local legends, agents exploring the town, cults, interviews with old timers who saw the beast, and a lot of thick atmosphere and tension that builds up to the first encounter with the Crooked Man.
